extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (U.S. citizens: current students, non-students, artists; and guidance for professors/administrators and non-U.S. applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Official program guidance describing types of Fulbright U.S. Student awards and applicant eligibility, application channels, special-program requirements, and procedural deadlines. Focus is on deciding which award type and whether an applicant is eligible and how to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Current U.S. Student
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there. Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. Citizen (not a student)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. The Getting Started page provides information on eligibility and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Artists (creative & performing arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts; arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience (typically 7 years or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / Application channel — U.S. Professors/Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support students applying for a U.S. Student Program award, professors/administrators should connect with the Fulbright Program Adviser at their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / Application channel — Non U.S. Citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States must apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in their home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.S. applicants should consult the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program for relevant opportunities and procedures in their home country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award type — Fulbright Study/Research Award
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright Study/Research Award is the traditional award opportunity where a candidate designs a proposal for a specific country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should read the Country Summaries for more information about country-specific opportunities and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award type — English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright English Teaching Assistant programs place grantees in schools overseas to supplement local English language instruction and to provide a native speaker presence in the classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should view the countries offering English Teaching Assistant Awards to determine availability and country-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Program — Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health (eligibility & purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships are offered in partnership with the Fogarty International Center, NIH, to promote expansion of research in public health and clinical research in resource-limited settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To participate applicants must be a U.S. citizen and: "By start of the program year, fellows must be an MD (and other professional degree) student who has completed their 3rd year of a Ph.D. candidate that has completed their master’s level requirements (i.e., post-qualifying exam)." The Fogarty program includes NIH support to the research training site, possible orientation at NIH, and a pre-departure orientation in Washington, DC. Other basic requirements and application process are the same as for any Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research Grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Program — Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program (selection focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program seeks proposals that undertake an in-depth examination of globally relevant issues as an add-on to the Fulbright Open Study/Research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects must incorporate science, storytelling, and/or education, and must align with one or more of National Geographic Society’s six focus areas: Ocean, Land, Wildlife, Human Histories and Cultures, Space, or Planetary Health. Successful applicants receive standard Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research benefits plus additional grant funds and access to National Geographic resources; the Society expects to select up to five applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional experience expectation (non-enrolled applicants & arts candidates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-enrolled applicants and arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience (typically 7 years or less) in the fields in which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with substantially more professional experience are encouraged to consider the Fulbright Scholar Program instead of the U.S. Student Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement — Application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: National deadline for the 2027-2028 competition is Tuesday October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must observe the published national and country/post-specific deadlines; check the program pages and Country Summaries for any variations.
